lines: [Empty stone room — close baritone, boot heel, acoustic, distant pump organ]
[Verse 1 — stark and restrained; acoustic guitar and faint organ]
They held the trial without me.
Let the rumor testify.
The folks who claimed to know me
Bought the worst and called it right.
They called ambition fantasy,
Called surrender growing wise;
Smiled and said, “We’re proud of you,”
With disappointment in their eyes.
The folks I took to be my north stars
Kept pointing at the ground.
Told me I could be damn near anything
As long as I stayed down.
[Pre-Chorus — low baritone guitar and upright bass enter]
They passed around the sentence.
Nobody named the crime.
I signed beneath their verdict
And agreed to serve the time.
[Chorus - Chain-gang stomp enters; restrained gospel responses]
They threw the stones.
I built the walls.
Packed their verdicts in the mortar,
Put their voices on the beat,
Gave their doubt the guardhouse
And their fear the master key.
I became my own correction.
Kept enforcing what they believed.
They cast me out in passing—
I spent years refusing to leave.
[Verse 2 — heavier boot-stomp pulse; tremolo guitar and baritone guitar]
I learned the torch, the wrench, the hammer.
Learned what holds and why it bends.
I could trace a failed connection,
Find the break and make it mend.
But couldn’t trust my own direction
Past the week or month ahead.
I built for everybody else
And left my own life on the page.
A good man waiting to feel worthy
Is still a good man in a cage.
I wanted love without suspicion,
Work that carried my own name;
A future chosen on its merits,
Not inherited fear and shame.
I wanted to become the man
I kept advising me to be—
But preaching freedom through the bars
Was close enough for me.
[Pre-Chorus — pressure rising; organ swells beneath the vocal]
A cage can feel like conscience
When you’ve worn it half your life.
Fear can sound exactly like wisdom
When it speaks in a trusted voice.
[Chorus — thunderous drums enter, but hold back the full release]
They threw the stones.
I built the walls.
Packed their verdicts in the mortar,
Put their voices on the beat,
Gave their doubt the guardhouse
And their fear the master key.
I became my own correction.
Kept enforcing what they believed.
They cast me out in passing—
I spent years refusing to leave.
[Verse 3 — pull back; tense acoustic, pedal steel and distant heartbeat]
For years I felt the floorboards shifting,
Heard the sentence losing weight.
Something living kept insisting
I was more than what they’d named.
Then sickness came and cleared the courtroom,
Took the witness, judge and chair.
The second time it stood me upright
With nobody left sitting there.
Just before we left for Arizona,
I walked the length of every lie;
Saw the stones were only stones,
Not commandments from on high.
I came at last upon the doorway,
Certain iron held it tight.
Laid one hand upon the handle—
[Total silence]
Then every damn thing goes quiet.
[Long pause]
[Bridge — nearly spoken; voice and acoustic only]
No tunnel underneath me.
No dynamite or chase.
I finally caught the jailer.
The bastard had my face.
[Heartbeat returns; pump organ rises]
I asked him for the reason.
He handed me the past.
I said, “That might explain the walls.
It doesn’t make them last.”
[Slow build; bass, organ and guitar feedback]
I learned plenty in that prison.
Paid in years I couldn’t spare.
The education may be useful.
The tuition wasn’t fair.
[Final Chorus — massive cinematic desert rock; thunderous live drums, tremolo guitars and raw gospel responses]
They threw the stones.
I built the walls.
Both accounts are coming due.
My hands don’t make them innocent.
Their hands don’t choose what I do.
I revoke the old conviction.
I won’t serve another day.
There was never any justice
In becoming my own cage.
[Prison Break Refrain — expansive and defiant; wordless choir and soaring pedal steel]
No sirens in the midnight.
No searchlight found my face.
No guards were running after me.
No gunfire shook the place.
I put my hand against the door
And felt a lifetime give way.
The lock had never held me.
[Full-band stop]
This is my prison break.
[Instrumental release — widescreen guitar and pedal steel over enormous drums]
[Spoken-word Outro — calm, deep baritone over sustained organ, steel and cinematic swell]
Let the walls repeat their verdict.
Let the empty guardhouse stare.
I took the life they said was foolish
And carried it out into the air.
The cell looked small behind me.
The sky refused an end.
[Music falls away]
I drew one last breath as my own jailer—
And let it out a free man.
[One final pedal-steel answer; long fading chord]
